summary:
What did you develop?

We Sent Them is an interactive web film where fifteen NASA machines tell their own stories in first person, including Eagle, the Apollo 17 Lunar Rover, Viking 1, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight and Ingenuity. Each describes how it was sent, worked and went silent. The film combines real NASA photographs, 3D scenes, an original score and voices recorded by our team. The Archive, an interactive tool, maps where each machine rests, compares planned and actual mission lifespans, and explains why each went silent.

How does it address the challenge?

It tells the story of equipment left on the Moon and Mars through the equipment itself, using real dates, places and last transmissions. The film makes people feel it. The Archive lets them explore the facts.

Why is it important?

Most people don't know these machines are still out there. They aren't junk. They are humanity's first footprints beyond Earth, and many far outlived their missions: Opportunity was built for ninety days and worked for almost fifteen years. Remembering them honours the people behind them and inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
Our project, is an interactive film, which covers the story of/and through the lens of some lander, rovers, and satellites that were sent by NASA, and are now decommissioned.

It personifies the lander, rovers, and satellites, so normal people can also feel connected to them as much as the scientists do.

We used html, css, ffmpeg and other resources, we coded in VS Code, with some help from Claude Code (SI) to develop this project.

We make it in an interactive film format, which is a mix of traditional and modern techniques and technology.

We consider the true story, and used our poetry and personification skills, to enhance emotion.
